blueprint_concepts: Sum of products of binomial coefficients (sum of C_r.C_(r+k))
solution_full: Put $k=j-i$; the condition $0\le i<j\le6$ means $1\le k\le6$ and $0\le i\le6-k$. So the double sum is $\sum_{k=1}^{6}k\,S_{k}$ with $S_{k}=\sum_{i=0}^{6-k}\binom{6}{i}\binom{6}{i+k}$.
Since $\binom{6}{i+k}=\binom{6}{6-k-i}$, $S_{k}$ is the coefficient of $x^{6-k}$ in $(1+x)^{6}(1+x)^{6}=(1+x)^{12}$, i.e. $S_{k}=\binom{12}{6-k}=\binom{12}{6+k}$.
Check by a closed form: $\sum_{k\ge1}k\binom{2n}{n+k}=\dfrac{n}{2}\binom{2n}{n}$; with $n=6$, $3\cdot924=2772$.
(Option (A) is half the answer and option (B) is $\binom{12}{6}$; option (D) double counts ordered pairs.)
originality_note: New: a double sum over i<j weighted by the gap j-i, which regroups by the gap into sums of products C_i C_(i+k) = C(12, 6+k) and then a weighted single sum (way 5). Closest known: sum over i<j of C_i C_j. Different because: the weight j - i forces grouping by the gap rather than the symmetry trick.

concept_use.Double Summations in Binomial Coefficien: The double sum over 0 <= i < j <= 6 is regrouped by k = j - i into a single sum over k.
concept_use.Sum of products of binomial coefficients: Each inner sum is a sum of products C(6,i) C(6,i+k) = C(12,6+k).

key_step: Regroup the double sum by the gap k = j - i and use sum C_i C_(i+k) = C(12, 6+k).
justification: Standard regrouping and the Vandermonde-type product sum, then six terms of arithmetic; a routine multi-step chain. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q1 (L2, counting with several sets).
